uncited: Reads an Wavefront OBJ file, extracts vertex coordinates and face indices, and ensures all polygons are triangulated.

It differs from its parent [PLY Mesh Loader & Normal Calculator](2859-ply-mesh-loader-normal-calculator.md) by parsing a different file format (ASCII text with specific token-based structure) and explicitly handling polygon-to-triangle conversion as a core requirement for volume rendering pipelines.
Initialize a reader configuration object.
Call the parse method with the file path and configuration.
Extract the vertex positions from the reader's internal storage.
Extract the face indices from the reader's internal storage.
If `true`, polygons are split into triangles.
- **Non-manifold geometry:** OBJ files may contain non-manifold edges or vertices.
The loader does not inherently fix topology; it only ensures triangulation.
The `tinyobj` library typically returns 0-based indices internally or handles the conversion.
If using raw parsing, indices must be adjusted by subtracting 1.
- **Missing normals/texcoords:** The loader extracts positions and faces.
Normals and texture coordinates are optional in OBJ and may not be present.
Writes a 3D mesh to an OBJ file, supporting optional per-vertex RGB colors.
If RGB colors are not provided, write `v x y z\n`.
- **Time Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of vertices and faces $O(V + F)$ for parsing.
Triangulation adds overhead proportional to the number of non-triangle faces.
- **Memory Complexity:** Linear $O(V + F)$ to store the mesh data.
Automatic triangulation simplifies downstream volume rendering.
Parsing speed depends on the implementation; `tinyobj` is efficient but not the fastest possible for massive files.
Originated from the Wavefront Technologies .obj file format, widely used in 3D modeling.
